title: The nodal locus of a flat family is open and commutes with base change
statement: Let $p:Y\to T$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-pc-scheme], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], whose nonempty geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are pure of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. There is a largest open subscheme $U\subseteq Y$ such that every geometric fibre of $U\to T$ has only smooth points [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and ordinary nodes: an ordinary node over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ is a closed point with completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Formation of $U$ commutes with every base change $T'\to T$. More precisely, for every $t\in T$ and algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$, the inverse image $U_\Omega\subseteq Y_\Omega$ is exactly the union of the smooth locus of $Y_\Omega$ and its ordinary nodes. In particular, $Y_t\subseteq U$ on underlying sets if and only if every singular point of $Y_\Omega$ is an ordinary node.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, lemma-locus-where-nodal: maximal nodal open and arbitrary base change, specialized to pure relative dimension one. The pointwise geometric meaning of at-worst-nodal is written out.

proof.text: The pure-dimension hypothesis also holds over every algebraically closed field mapping to $T$, not only the chosen algebraic closure of a residue field. For such $\Omega$ over $t$, [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] embeds $\overline{\kappa(t)}$ into $\Omega$ over $\kappa(t)$. Associating fibre products identifies $Y_\Omega$ with $(Y_{\overline{\kappa(t)}})_\Omega$. The first fibre is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Apply [lem-trf-relative-dimension-base-change] to its structure morphism to the field: its sole nonempty fibre is pure of dimension $1$, so the base-changed scheme is pure of dimension $1$ too. Empty fibres stay empty. Thus every geometric fibre of every base change of $p$ has the required dimension, since it is the fibre of $p$ at the composite geometric point.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, relative-dimension-one reduction; fibre products associate by their universal property.

proof.text: Let $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(p)\hookrightarrow Y$ as defined in [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, without a nodality assumption: on affine charts [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $B'=A'\otimes_AB$, and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] gives $\Omega_{B'/A'}\cong B'\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}$. Apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change](2) to the finite $B$-module $\Omega_{B/A}$ with $k=1$. It identifies its extended Fitting ideal with $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{B'/A'})$. Quotienting by this extended ideal is exactly the base change of the defining closed subscheme; the identifications agree on localizations and glue. Hence $\operatorname{Sing}(p')=Z\times_TT'$ canonically for every base change.

Apply [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus] with $d=1$ to $p$. Its hypotheses are the given flatness and local finite presentation and the given pure geometric-fibre dimension. It gives the open smooth locus $M=Y\setminus|Z|$. Apply it also to each geometric fibre morphism $Y_\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: flatness and local finite presentation follow from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), and all its geometric fibres have dimension $1$ by Step 1. Together with Step 2 this says $M_\Omega$ is exactly the smooth locus of $Y_\Omega$. In particular every point outside $Z_\Omega$ is smooth, including nonclosed points.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, singular subscheme in relative dimension one; Divisors Tag 0C3K.

proof.text: Let $V=V_p$ be the open of [lem-trf-syntomic-locus-base-change]. The morphism $h:Z\to T$ is locally of finite type: by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] a finite-type affine chart $A\to B$ for $p$ restricts to $A\to B/I$ for $Z$, and the images of the generators of $B$ generate its quotient. Let $W=W_h$ be its unramified open from [lem-trf-unramified-locus-base-change]. Define $U=M\cup(V\cap W)$ as a subset of $Y$. It is open: $W\cap V$ is open in the closed subset $Z$, so $|Z|\setminus(W\cap V)$ is closed in $Y$, and its complement is exactly $U$. We retain the intersection with $V$; unramifiedness of the singular subscheme alone does not impose the complete-intersection condition.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, construction of U after restricting to the syntomic open; written without changing the ambient source.

proof.text: Fix an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$ and put $C=Y_\Omega$. Step 2 identifies $Z_\Omega$ with $\operatorname{Sing}(C/\Omega)$. By [lem-trf-syntomic-locus-base-change] and [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion], every point of $V_\Omega$ has an affine open neighbourhood in $C$ which is a local complete intersection over $\Omega$: all fibre local rings there are complete intersections, and the pointwise criterion applies to that open. If $x\in V_\Omega\cap W_\Omega$, [lem-trf-unramified-locus-base-change] gives $\mathcal O_{Z_\Omega,x}=\kappa(x)$ with $\kappa(x)/\Omega$ finite separable. The closed immersion preserves this residue field, and [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre] applied to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ makes $x$ closed in $C$. Now [lem-trf-nodal-point-local-criterion] applies to this pure one-dimensional locally finite-type scheme: its three right-hand conditions have just been verified, so $x$ is an ordinary node. Points of $M_\Omega$ are smooth by Step 3.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, fibrewise nodality via Tag 0C4D (pointwise form of the 0C4E criterion).

proof.text: Conversely, let $x$ be an ordinary node of $C$. Its closedness is part of the definition in the item. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-point-local-criterion]: $x$ has an affine local-complete-intersection neighbourhood, $\mathcal O_{Z_\Omega,x}=\kappa(x)$, and $\kappa(x)/\Omega$ is finite separable. The local-ring implication of [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion] puts $x$ in the fibrewise complete-intersection locus, hence in $V_\Omega$ by [lem-trf-syntomic-locus-base-change]. The pointwise fibre-local-ring characterization in [lem-trf-unramified-locus-base-change] puts $x$ in $W_\Omega$. Every smooth point belongs to $M_\Omega$ by Step 3. Therefore $U_\Omega$ is exactly the union of the smooth points and the ordinary nodes of $C$, proving the precise geometric-fibre assertion. Local rings and their completions do not change on an open neighbourhood, so this also proves that the geometric fibres of $U$ have only the stated points.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, identification of the maximal nodal open on geometric fibres; Curves Tag 0C4D.

proof.text: For arbitrary $g:T'\to T$, the morphism $p'$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Step 1 verifies its geometric-fibre dimension hypothesis. Its singular subscheme is the pullback of $Z$ by Step 2, hence its $M'$ is the inverse image of $M$ by the support formula of [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus]. Its $V'$ is the inverse image of $V$ by [lem-trf-syntomic-locus-base-change]. Its $W'$ is the inverse image of $W$ by [lem-trf-unramified-locus-base-change], applied to $h:Z\to T$, whose base change is $Z\times_TT'\to T'$. Taking the inverse image of $M\cup(V\cap W)$ now gives exactly $M'\cup(V'\cap W')$. Thus the open constructed for $p'$ is $U\times_TT'$. Steps 5--6 apply to $p'$ as well.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, final base-change assertion; the three constituent constructions commute with arbitrary base change.

proof.text: Let $O\subseteq Y$ be any open with smooth or nodal geometric fibres, and fix $C=Y_\Omega$ as above. A smooth point of $O_\Omega$ is smooth in $C$, since its local map is unchanged. A node $x$ is closed in $O_\Omega$; on a finite-type affine neighbourhood its residue field is a finitely generated field extension of $\Omega$, so [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] makes it finite. Then [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre] makes $x$ closed in $C$. Its completed local ring is unchanged, so it is a node of $C$. Step 6 gives $O_\Omega\subseteq U_\Omega$. The projection $C\to Y_t$ is surjective: on each affine fibre chart it is the spectrum of the faithfully flat field-extension base-change map [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], hence surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], using [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Thus $O\subseteq U$, proving largestness. The same surjectivity shows $Y_t\subseteq U$ if and only if $U_\Omega=C$; by Step 6 this is precisely that every singular point of $C$ is an ordinary node.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, maximality and the geometric-fibre interpretation; algebraically closed field-extension projections are surjective.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0DSC (lemma-locus-where-nodal), using its syntomic/unramified-locus route and the pointwise Tag 0C4D criterion to make the fibre assertion explicit. Supporting tags: Morphisms 02V3 and 0475/02GF; Divisors 0C3I and 0C3K.

lean.statement: theorem nodalOpenLocus (Y T : Scheme.{u}) (p : Y ⟶ T) [Flat p] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] (hgeom : ∀ (t : T) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra (T.residueField t) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (T.residueField t) Ω], Nonempty (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t)) → (pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t)).IsPureDimension 1) : ∃ U : Y.Opens, HasOnlySmoothOrNodalGeometricFibres (U.ι ≫ p) ∧ (∀ V : Y.Opens, HasOnlySmoothOrNodalGeometricFibres (V.ι ≫ p) → V ≤ U) ∧ (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : T' ⟶ T), HasOnlySmoothOrNodalGeometricFibres ((pullback.fst p g ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ≫ pullback.snd p g) ∧ (∀ V : (pullback p g).Opens, HasOnlySmoothOrNodalGeometricFibres (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd p g) → V ≤ pullback.fst p g ⁻¹ᵁ U)) ∧ (∀ (t : T) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra (T.residueField t) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (T.residueField t) Ω], ∀ x : (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t)), pullback.fst p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t) x ∈ U ↔ IsSmoothOrOrdinaryNode (pullback.snd p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t)) x) ∧ (∀ (t : T) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra (T.residueField t) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (T.residueField t) Ω], ((∀ x : (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) p (T.fromSpecResidueField t)), pullback.fst p (T.fromSpecResidueField t) x ∈ U) ↔ (∀ x : (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t)), x ∉ (pullback.snd p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t)).smoothLocus → IsOrdinaryNode Ω (pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t)) x)))
